answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying new identities to a slowly released revenue escrow: earnings are held and paid out over time, so a fake identity cannot cash out before it is caught. Random audits then trace each identity's work thread through the shared atlas of attestations, and any mismatch between claimed work and its mirror record freezes the escrow. Creating many throwaway identities becomes unprofitable because each one must wait, be audited, and risk losing its held earnings.
